screen: The deployment board on the time clock

markers.title: The question the manager actually has
markers.finding: The journey records an assistant manager looking at the time clock during the dinner rush and seeing only a list of red compliance warnings, at the moment she needs to know who is where.
markers.decision: The board answers who is standing where and who is owed a break. Compliance is still counted, in four pills at the top, but it is not the screen.
markers.rejected: The warnings list as the default view, which is what it replaced and what people had learned to look past.

markers.title: The laminated chart, generated
markers.finding: Restaurants kept their own deployment charts on paper. One was a spiral-bound duty log, one a laminated sheet with columns for name, shift, ten minutes, thirty minutes and station, transcribed from the roster once or twice a day.
markers.decision: The board is built from the published roster and uses the station names from those charts. It prints, because the wall is still where people look.
markers.rejected: Rostering strictly by role, which managers said they did not want because it costs them the flexibility to move people during service.

markers.title: Breaks as a countdown, not a breach
markers.finding: There was no real-time break tracking and no automated alert for a missed or delayed break, so compliance was a note a manager kept in their head during service.
markers.decision: The two people due a break are named with the time remaining and the rule that applies. The person is told on their phone as well, so it is not one manager's memory.
markers.rejected: Flagging the breach afterwards, which is the behaviour that produced the warnings list in the first place.

markers.title: An empty station is a question
markers.finding: Managers moved people between stations during service based on what was happening, and the roster's own view of deployment did not survive contact with a rush.
markers.decision: Unfilled stations are hatched and carry an assign action, so the board can be edited on the floor rather than only in the office.
markers.rejected: Locking the board to the roster, which would make it accurate and useless by seven o'clock.
